body:
I am against adding onClick (only) because even if it solves the "click" use case, it will easily get out of control:

* I want to listen for double click
* I want to listen for drag event
* I want to listen for mouseenter mouseleave
* I want to read some data attributes I just set in my template
* ..

I do not see onDomNodeAdded as something over engineered while we can see onClick as being too narrow on the API it exposes.

The current usecase you faced might be seen at the "only usecase" but I fear they are more to take into account.

We need to think more and more in term of pluggable API endpoints giving power to everyone. Answering beginners question like "How to add a click to every hit element" belongs to a guide and not a dedicated API entry point.

onDomNodeAdded is actually already doable by using React refs (those can be callbacks) https://facebook.github.io/react/docs/more-about-refs.html

If it's doable then let's do it.

Careful also because neither onClick nor onDomNodeAdded will work with our "allItems" template.
